'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023-present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza war hostage crisis]], [[Israeli–Palestinian peace process]]
****The [[United States]] releases a 20-point [[ceasefire]] [[Donald Trump's September 2025 Gaza Strip proposal|proposal]] to end the [[Gaza war]], to which [[Israel]] agrees. The proposal includes the immediate end of [[military operation]]s inside the [[Gaza Strip]] and the release of all living hostages within 72 hours. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-forces-advance-ahead-trump-netanyahu-gaza-war-talks-2025-09-29/ (Reuters)]
***[[2025 Gaza City offensive]]
****At least 39 [[Palestinians]] are killed in [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] attacks across the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/9/29/live-israel-keeps-pummeling-gaza-ahead-of-trump-netanyahu-meeting (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***A [[Houthi]] [[anti-ship missile]] attack on [[Netherlands|Dutch]]-flagged cargo ship ''Minervagracht'' injures two people and forces the crew to abandon the ship. [https://apnews.com/article/yemen-houthis-gulf-aden-ship-fire-missile-1a42485ac4ab29188ed1ea85414aba48 (AP)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Ukraine]] allegedly shoots down a [[Russian Air Force]] [[Mil Mi-8]] on combat search and rescue duties with an [[First-person view (radio control)|FPV]] drone in Nadaeyvka, [[Pokrovsk Raion]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], Ukraine, killing several people and injuring several others. [https://asn.flightsafety.org/wikibase/547843 (ASN)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Unidentified gunmen kill at least twelve [[Nigerian Hunter & Forest Security Service|forest security guards]] in Oke-Ode, [[Kwara State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-attack-forest-guards-kwara-09603b3889d34814159c10802a36fe43 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[German economic crisis (2022–present)|German economic crisis]], [[Workplace impact of artificial intelligence]]
**[[Germany|German]] airline [[Lufthansa]] announces they will cut 4,000 [[management|administrative]] positions by 2030 and replace them with [[artificial intelligence]] and [[digitization]] processes. [https://www.dw.com/en/lufthansa-to-shed-4000-jobs-with-help-from-ai/a-74173278 (DW)]
*[[Video games in the United States|American]] [[video game company]] [[Electronic Arts]] (EA) agrees to be acquired by a group of private investors, including [[Silver Lake (investment firm)|Silver Lake]], the [[Public Investment Fund]] of [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[Affinity Partners]], in a deal valued at $55 billion. The transaction, which will take EA [[Privately held company|private]], constitutes the largest [[leveraged buyout]] on record. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-29/ea-agrees-to-sale-in-largest-leveraged-buyout-on-record (Bloomberg News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**At least one person is killed as [[Tropical Storm Imelda (2025)|Tropical Storm Imelda]] makes [[landfall]] in [[the Bahamas]] and [[Cuba]]. [https://apnews.com/article/weather-hurricane-humberto-tropical-storm-imelda-94d436e55831bd7d0b95c0432045d03f (AP)]
*Eight people are killed and 14 others are injured after a bus overturns in [[Samalut]], [[Minya Governorate]], [[Egypt]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-ae/news/other/8-killed-14-injured-in-deadly-bus-crash-in-egypts-minya/ar-AA1NvzI2?ocid=BingNewsSerp (MSN)]
*Three students are killed, 38 more are missing and 77 injured after the collapse of a ''[[pesantren]]'' in [[Sidoarjo Regency|Sidoarjo]], [[East Java]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/30/school-collapse-in-indonesia-leaves-one-student-dead-38-missing (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Namibia]] deploys 540 [[Namibian Defence Force|soldiers]] to contain [[wildfire]]s that have burned more than {{cvt|770,000|ha|km2|abbr=on}}, about a third of [[Etosha National Park]], along with surrounding land. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/29/africa/etosha-namibia-wildfire-scli-intl (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–United States relations]], [[South Africa–United States relations]], [[Human trafficking in Brazil]], [[Human trafficking in South Africa]]
**The [[United States]] places [[Brazil]] and [[South Africa]] on the Tier 2 watchlist of its [[Trafficking in Persons Report]], citing insufficient progress in combating [[human trafficking]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-puts-brazil-south-africa-human-trafficking-watch-list-2025-09-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[China–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]] begins a [[pilot program]] allowing [[Visa policy of South Korea|visa-free]] entry for [[Chinese nationality law|Chinese]] tourist groups of three or more for stays of up to 15 days. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/south-korea-pilot-visa-free-entry-chinese-tourist-groups-cctv-reports-2025-09-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Colombia–United States relations]]
**[[Colombia]]n [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Colombia)|foreign minister]] [[Rosa Villavicencio]] renounces her [[United States visa]] in response to the [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]]'s cancellation of [[President of Colombia|President]] [[Gustavo Petro]]'s visa. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/colombia-foreign-minister-visa-usa-trump-b2836140.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Hungary–Ukraine relations]], [[Telecommunications in Hungary]]
**[[Hungary]] [[Block (Internet)|blocks]] access to 12 [[List of newspapers in Ukraine|Ukrainian news]] [[Online newspaper|websites]] to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] [[Ukraine]]'s earlier ban on several [[Hungarian-language]] [[Web portal|portals]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/hungary-blocks-12-ukrainian-news-sites-tit-for-tat-2025-09-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russia]]n [[President of Russia|president]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a law denouncing and leaving the [[European Convention for the Prevention of Torture and Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment|European Convention against Torture]], after the country left the [[Council of Europe]] in 2022. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-exits-european-anti-torture-convention-2025-09-29/ (Reuters)] [https://mezha.net/eng/bukvy/russia-denounces-european-convention-against-torture-ending-international-monitoring/ (Mezha)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Moroccan Gen Z protests]]
**[[Morocco|Moroccan]] [[Sûreté Nationale (Morocco)|police]] detain dozens of people on the third consecutive day of [[Generation Z|Gen Z]]-led protests across the country against [[Corruption in Morocco|government corruption]] in prioritizing [[2030 World Cup|public image]] over [[Health in Morocco|healthcare]] and [[Education in Morocco|education crises]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/morocco-police-detain-dozens-in-gen-z-protests/a-74182240 (DW)]
*[[Capital punishment in China]], [[China–Myanmar relations]]
**The [[intermediate people's court]] in [[Wenzhou]], [[Zhejiang province]], [[China]], sentences 11 people, including three from a powerful family in [[Kokang]], [[Myanmar]], to [[death sentence|death]] for [[murder]], running an [[illegal gambling]] and [[scam center|scamming]] [[crime syndicate]]. The court also sentences 12 other people to prison sentences between five and 24 years. [https://apnews.com/article/china-myanmar-court-death-sentence-syndicate-63b170ca31cd9b37a6817858f6c6b0bb (AP)]
*[[Capital punishment in Iran]]
**[[Iran]] executes a man convicted of being a spy for [[Israel|Israeli]] spy agency [[Mossad]] working on sensitive telecommunications projects and providing information on routes for importing electronic devices.[https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgn078zlgro (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Malagasy protests]]
**[[Madagascar]] [[President of Madagascar|president]] [[Andry Rajoelina]] dismisses [[Prime Minister of Madagascar|Prime Minister]] [[Christian Ntsay]] and [[Fifth Ntsay Government|his cabinet]] following protests over [[Energy crisis|electricity]] and [[water shortage]]s that left dozens dead and injured, while announcing an [[interim government]] until a replacement is appointed. **[[Seychelles]] will hold a second-round presidential election after neither of the leading candidates, incumbent [[President of Seychelles|president]] [[Wavel Ramkalawan]] and opposition leader [[Patrick Herminie]], obtains 50% of the vote. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c36kre10g8eo (BBC News)]
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**[[Ako Bicol]] representative [[Zaldy Co]] resigns from the [[Philippine]] [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] after being implicated in alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] involving [[flood control]] projects. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/nation/2025/9/29/zaldy-co-resigns-as-house-representative-amid-flood-control-scandal-1600 (ABS-CBN News)]
*[[Human rights in Afghanistan]], [[Internet in Afghanistan]]
**The [[Taliban]] imposes a nationwide [[Internet outage|internet blackout]] in [[Afghanistan]] to "prevent immorality", cutting [[Fiber-optic communication|fiber-optic services]] and reducing connectivity to about 14% of normal levels, according to monitoring group [[NetBlocks]]. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-taliban-internet-crackdown-dfdda5c1ef1d29124db4649414584c6e (AP)]
